key_insight: Bayesian inference on photoluminescence imaging and drift-diffusion simulations can localize perovskite solar-cell degradation to specific interfaces or the bulk, rather than treating it as uniform damage.
engineering_relevance: This enables targeted durability engineering by identifying whether hole-transport, electron-transport, or bulk regions are driving performance loss and how passivation can mitigate it.
method: Photoluminescence imaging of fully fabricated devices
Drift-diffusion simulations linked to Bayesian parameter inference
Time-resolved mapping of optoelectronic degradation during 70 °C full-spectrum light aging
evidence_signal: The abstract reports inferred spatial parameter maps that evolve during aging and reveal strong non-uniform degradation, with the largest losses concentrated at perovskite/transport-layer interfaces and reduced by amino-silane passivation.
watch_item: The inferred maps depend on model assumptions and measurement quality, so incorrect simulation priors or limited imaging resolution could bias the attribution of degradation mechanisms.
paper_title: Disentangling the origin of degradation in perovskite solar cells via optical imaging and Bayesian inference
